typical_visual_logic: One or more lines over time.
typical_risk: Readers may overread frequency as cultural importance, universality, or first use.
source_boundary_handling: Usually source boundary is present but visually secondary to the curve.
words_over_time_response: Keeps frequency as Signal, then surrounds it with Attestation, Context, Boundary, and Rights.

strength: Strong at lexical authority and attested sense history.
typical_risk: Weak at public visibility, comparative trend, and visual relation among evidence types.
source_boundary_handling: Source authority is strong but often compressed into editorial format.
words_over_time_response: Uses Attestation as one column rather than the whole argument.

typical_visual_logic: Lists occurrences, metadata, snippets, concordance lines.
typical_risk: Hard for public readers to synthesize; source and rights can become workflow details.
source_boundary_handling: Source boundary may be precise but not visually explanatory.
words_over_time_response: Turns selected corpus evidence into Context and Rights layers.

typical_risk: Can smooth uncertainty and make history look too linear.
source_boundary_handling: Source limits often appear in small print or not at all.
words_over_time_response: Uses timelines only when boundary labels and variant policies stay visible.

typical_risk: May imply objectivity through interface polish and numeric density.
source_boundary_handling: Often treats data provenance as metadata rather than argument.
words_over_time_response: Treats provenance and non-claims as central visual material.

typical_visual_logic: Frequency, attestation, variants, context, boundaries, and rights arranged as co-present evidence roles.
strength: Makes heterogeneous evidence types visible together.
typical_risk: Can increase visual density and cognitive load.
source_boundary_handling: Source boundary is part of the composition, not only citation apparatus.
words_over_time_response: Positions visual structure as epistemic structure.
